title: Change Pratica software and contracts
summary: Modify Pratica's negotiation mechanics, steward requester, integration composition, conformance review, SQLite state, CLI, packaging, tests, documentation, or published contracts while preserving opaque terms and product authority boundaries.
use_when: Pratica code, schema, tools, prompts, sources, CLI or JSON behavior, state, recovery, packaging, release workflow, documentation, or Chancery bundle is being changed.
do_not_use_when: The request is ordinary use or operation of the installed Pratica CLI.
Release publication or installed deployment has not been separately authorized.
The proposed change would make Pratica interpret product-contract semantics, mutate target systems, or automatically discover scopes without a new reviewed contract.
outcome: A minimal tested Pratica change whose four slices, exact protocol, opaque terms, requester lifecycle, persistent state, recovery, privacy, installation, and published contracts agree.
effects: Modifies Pratica source, tests, schema, product documentation, packaging, release tooling, or product-owned Chancery contracts.
Requester changes can alter retained prompts, frozen source disclosure, immutable tool registrations, correlations, permissions, and recovery.
Schema changes can affect private persistent agreement history; release and deployment remain separate effects.
authority: Pratica owns negotiation and review domain state; target products own their implementation and contracts; Nucleus owns shared agent execution.
The Nucleus requester contract and operator manual own shared invocation, mailbox, recovery, compatibility, and maintenance requirements.
Chancery owns provider schema and discovery while Pratica owns the truth of its published capability claims.
success: Architecture, CLI, data model, installation, Nucleus operator facts, code, tests, and Chancery contracts agree on every affected behavior.

Tests preserve exact Markdown bytes, distinct offer identity, stale-base exclusion, assent staleness, immutable seals, basis guards, source bounds, tool-call idempotency, and runtime/domain-success separation as affected.
Packaging retains exact content identity, selector ownership, foreign-state refusal, database non-interference, and rollback.
pratica/ci.sh completes green offline with synthetic fixtures.
failure_and_recovery: Do not weaken validation, interpret contract prose in the database, resurrect stale assent by digest, rewrite sealed history, or infer implementation success from a review.
Persistent change requires an explicit migration, old-state fixture, quiescent backup, and database-aware rollback.
Immutable tool meaning changes require new schema and toolset identities with retained historical decoding.
privacy: Fixtures are synthetic and contain no real CRM terms, conversation body, target source, credentials, private paths, prompts, tool payloads, or negotiated state.
Diagnostics and packaging tests must remain body-free and release bundles must contain no Pratica database.
steps: Read Pratica instructions and exact architecture, CLI, data-model, installation, and Chancery contracts affected by the change.
Run the installed Nucleus manual before changing public behavior, state, requester, lifecycle, deployment, or compatibility.
Implement the smallest change with synthetic frozen sources and update every affected product and shared operator contract together.
Run pratica/ci.sh and then the complete Cell root gate; release and deployment remain separately authorized.
checkpoints: Terms remain exact opaque Markdown and offers remain complete immutable snapshots.
pratica/steward-response/1, pratica/composition-review/1, and pratica/conformance-review/1 retain exact immutable meanings or receive successor identities.
Model jobs retain workspace none, no shell/web/launch context, closed frozen source tools, one attempt, and no direct fallback.
Composition cannot mutate agreements and conformance cannot change or implement the target system.
adaptation: Add a logical steward scope by registering a versioned manifest rather than coupling the product to a target repository.
Add source kinds only with explicit identity, cutoff, bounds, privacy, and recovery semantics.
stop_when: A target fact cannot be obtained through an authorized bounded source snapshot.
A state, toolset, or cutover change lacks deterministic compatibility and recovery.
The change would acquire target-system mutation, automatic scope discovery, policy enforcement, or release-gate authority.
does_not_authorize: Running release.sh, which commits, tags, and pushes.
Deploying Pratica, initializing or deleting installed state, invoking a real Nucleus job, or changing CRM or another target system.

consumers.statement: An interactive contributor may change Pratica while preserving opaque terms, exact bases, bilateral protocol mechanics, restricted requester behavior, and synchronized public contracts.

preconditions.statement: The contributor has read Pratica instructions and semantics, affected public contracts, and Nucleus requester/operator contracts, with separate authority for release or deployment.

inputs.statement: Inputs are the requested scoped change, current Pratica source and contracts, exact selected documentation contracts, and synthetic frozen-source and fake-runtime fixtures.

outputs.statement: The output is the smallest synchronized protocol, state, requester, test, documentation, packaging, or provider change with Pratica and root CI green.

data_semantics.statement: Development preserves exact opaque Markdown, complete immutable offers, fixed parties, basis-bound assent and seals, advisory composition, evidence-only conformance, and target-product authority.

identity_and_units.statement: Existing protocol, offer, source, schema, toolset, requester, attempt, and agreement identities retain exact meanings unless explicit successors are introduced.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Completion covers every affected Pratica architecture, CLI, data model, requester fact, installation behavior, provider contract, synthetic test, and current CI result.

access.statement: Development uses the local repository filesystem and shell; tests use synthetic sources and fake Nucleus transport and disclose no real terms or target data.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Persistent changes require explicit migration, old-state fixture, quiescent backup, and database-aware rollback; tool meaning changes require immutable successor schemas and toolsets.

operational_limits.statement: The operation stays within a short-lived local CLI and stops before acquiring target mutation, automatic scope discovery, policy enforcement, or release-gate authority.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Development retains historical exact-byte decoding and explicit protocol compatibility; incompatible state or tool meaning receives a versioned successor rather than reinterpretation.

reliances.statement: Pratica development relies on its registered Semantics repository for maintained project terminology while source, tests, and product documentation remain authoritative for behavior.
Other selected entries remain documentation contracts and do not create a live Pratica, Nucleus, or target-system runtime reliance of the development operation.
